demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian cement industry has substantial long-term headroom given low per-capita consumption relative to global levels
- FY26 industry-wide cement volume recovery (production growth ~8.7%) driven by normalised government capital expenditure and resilient housing demand, after the election-related slowdown of FY25
- Growth in FY26 was led more by throughput than by pricing, with average cement prices up only about 2%
- Housing and infrastructure together account for close to 90% of domestic cement demand, keeping the sector linked to public investment and residential construction
- New Vizag (Thallapalem/Anakapalle) grinding unit, commissioned November 2025, strengthens Company's reach into eastern Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
- Favourable demand environment and pan-India dealer network support a positive medium-term outlook for the cement division
- RMC segment expected to record steady growth on continued urban construction
- Boards segment demand potential expanding on growing awareness and new applications, despite competition and substitute products
- Industry demand for cement and building materials projected to grow in mid-to-high single digits in FY27, driven by sustained public capex and resilient housing demand
- Operating margins in FY27 will remain sensitive to the pace of price increases and the price trajectory of coal, petcoke and freight, and to the absorption rate of newly commissioned industry capacity
- Boards, RMC and Energy divisions expected to deliver steady revenue contributions going forward
- JV with NCL Buildtek Limited secured an order valued at Rs. 1,863 crores from Andhra Pradesh State Housing Corporation Limited (APSHCL) for pre-painted GI steel window frames and GI powder-coated door frames; against this, only Rs. 46.07 crores of orders have been received and executed to date, and the JV is in the process of closure and dissolution

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company commissioned a new greenfield 0.66 MTPA cement grinding unit at Thallapalem, near Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh in November 2025, built on land owned by wholly owned subsidiary Tern Distilleries Private Limited; this raised overall cement production capacity from 3.30 MTPA to 4.00 MTPA and strengthens reach into eastern Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The Company is evaluating opportunities to add capacity in the Boards (Bison Panel) business given growing demand potential, though no specific project has been announced. In renewable energy, the Company commenced establishing a 130 MW Solar and Wind Hybrid project at Kuppanpuram, Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu, to be implemented in phases; Phase I (50 MW), intended to meet the bulk of the power requirement of the Mattapally plant through captive consumption, was approved by the Board for commissioning by February 2028.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: Pan-India dealer network supporting the cement division — evidence: about 2,400 dealers across nine states (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kerala, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Odisha), supported by a Dealer Welfare Trust established in 1986
- technology: Only domestic manufacturer of Cement Bonded Particle Boards, engineered via technical collaboration with Bison Werke, Germany — evidence: 'NCL is the only manufacturer of Cement Bonded Particle Boards in India, marketed as Bison Panel'
- cost position: Rising captive green power share reducing cement power costs — evidence: green power share of cement power drawn increased to 28% in FY26 from 23% in FY25, via 15.75 MW hydel, 8 MW waste heat recovery and 12.54 MW solar
- resource: Captive limestone mining lease held via subsidiary — evidence: Vishwamber Cements Limited was acquired primarily for its mining lease covering 322.06 acres of limestone-bearing land [planned — amalgamation into the Company pending statutory/regulatory approvals]

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Volatility in prices of key inputs — coal, petcoke, steel and freight — can pressure realisations and margins.
- Limited pricing power at a time of large industry capacity additions and consolidation by large players can compress realisations, particularly for medium-sized producers.
- Availability of new limestone mines at reasonable cost remains a constraint factor on capacity growth.
- Regional demand patterns and monsoon variability can affect volumes given the Company's southern-market concentration.
- In the Boards business, competition and the emergence of substitute products are ongoing challenges.
- Global events can affect market stability and introduce uncertainty into the industry outlook.
- The NCL Buildtek & NCL Industries JV has seen limited execution of its awarded order, continued operating losses, and is in the process of closure and dissolution, leading to a provision for diminution in the value of the Company's investment.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Sharpened focus on core operations (Cement, Boards, RMC, Energy) following strategic exit from the Doors business
- Ongoing cost efficiency measures and expanded deployment of low-cost renewable power to accelerate performance
- Strengthening the Boards (Bison Panel) business through enhanced branding initiatives, expanded market outreach, improved customer engagement and operational excellence
- Evaluating amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiaries (Tern Distilleries and Vishwamber Cements) with the Company to simplify corporate structure and make limestone mines captive
- Structurally reducing power cost and lowering carbon intensity through the 130 MW solar and wind hybrid renewable project

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
